scenario: What is the correct order of the Google Cloud resource hierarchy from top to bottom?
explanation: Google Cloud's hierarchy runs Organization, then folders, then projects, with resources inside projects. IAM and organization policies set higher up are inherited by everything below, so the order matters for where you grant access.

scenario: A new project needs to use the Compute Engine API. What must be done first?

options.text: Enable the API and link a billing account
Create a VPC peering connection to the default network
Request a quota increase for vCPUs in every region

explanation: Compute Engine calls only work once the API is enabled on the project, and most paid APIs also need an active billing account linked. Quota increases and service account keys come later, if at all.

refs.title: Enable and disable services | Service Usage
Enable, disable, or change billing for a project

scenario: Which command sets the default project for the gcloud CLI?

options.note: Not a valid way to set the CLI default.

explanation: gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID sets the default project for later commands. gcloud projects create makes a new project, and named configurations let you switch between accounts and projects.

refs.title: gcloud config set | Google Cloud SDK

scenario: A team wants a spending alert when a project reaches 80% of $1,000 per month. What should be configured?

options.text: A Cloud Billing budget with threshold rules
A quota limit on Compute Engine
An uptime check on the billing console
A log-based metric on billing log entries

explanation: A Cloud Billing budget with threshold rules (such as 80% of $1,000) sends alerts when spending reaches those percentages. Budgets only alert unless you automate action with Pub/Sub; quotas and uptime checks don't track spend.

refs.title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts | Cloud Billing

scenario: How can detailed billing data be analyzed with SQL?

options.text: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery
Download the monthly PDF invoice and import it

explanation: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery to analyze costs with SQL, using the standard or detailed usage cost exports. The PDF invoice and audit logs don't contain queryable cost data.

refs.title: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery

scenario: Which IAM role type should generally be avoided in production because it's very broad?

options.text: Basic roles like Owner, Editor and Viewer
Service agent roles granted by Google services

explanation: Basic roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) grant very broad permissions across services and should generally be avoided in production. Predefined and custom roles give fine-grained access.

refs.title: IAM roles and permissions index | IAM

scenario: A user needs to manage only Compute Engine instances in one project. Which role is best?
explanation: Grant the narrowest role at the lowest level that meets the need: roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1 on the project manages Compute Engine instances there without broader organization-wide access.

refs.title: IAM roles and permissions index | IAM

scenario: Where should IAM roles be granted to give a group access to all projects in the Finance department?
explanation: Roles granted on a folder are inherited by every project beneath it, so granting a group the role on the Finance folder covers all Finance projects. Doing it per VM or per bucket doesn't scale.

refs.title: IAM roles and permissions index | IAM

scenario: What's the recommended way to grant access to people?

options.text: Grant roles to Google groups, not individual users
Share one admin account among staff
Create service account keys for each person
Grant Owner to everyone temporarily, then remove it later

explanation: Grant roles to Google groups instead of individual users, which simplifies onboarding and offboarding. Shared accounts, per-person keys and temporary Owner grants all weaken accountability.

scenario: Which service manages user identities for a Google Cloud organization without Google Workspace?
explanation: Cloud Identity manages user identities and groups for an organization without Google Workspace, and can sync from Active Directory using Google Cloud Directory Sync.

scenario: A project hit a limit on the number of vCPUs in a region. What should the admin do?
explanation: When a project hits a regional vCPU limit, request a quota increase. Quotas protect against unexpected usage and can be raised on request; a new billing account or disabling the API doesn't help.

scenario: Which tool lets admins restrict resource locations to EU regions across all projects?

options.text: An organization policy with the resource locations constraint
An egress firewall rule blocking non-EU IP ranges
A VPC Service Controls perimeter only
A Cloud Billing budget per region

explanation: An organization policy with the resource locations constraint restricts where resources can be created, such as EU regions only, and is inherited down the hierarchy. Firewall rules and budgets don't restrict resource locations.

scenario: Which interface gives a browser-based shell with gcloud already installed?
explanation: Cloud Shell is a browser-based shell with gcloud preinstalled, an editor and persistent home storage. Cloud Run, Scheduler and Tasks are not shells.

scenario: Which billing roles allow linking a project to a billing account?

options.text: Billing Account User on the account and Project Billing Manager on the project
Viewer on the project and Billing Account Viewer on the account
Billing Account Costs Manager on the account only
options.note: Manages budgets, but cannot link projects alone.

explanation: Linking a project to billing needs Billing Account User on the billing account and Project Billing Manager (or equivalent) on the project. Viewers on either can't change the link.

refs.title: Enable, disable, or change billing for a project

scenario: Which command installs additional components like kubectl for the gcloud CLI?
explanation: gcloud components install kubectl adds optional components to the gcloud CLI. If gcloud was installed through an OS package manager, install components with that package manager instead.

scenario: Which labels best help track costs by environment and team?

options.text: Key-value labels like env=prod and team=web on resources
Long resource names that include the date and team

explanation: Key-value labels like env=prod and team=web on resources appear in billing exports, so you can filter and group costs by environment and team. Long names or per-VM billing accounts are impractical.

refs.title: Create and update labels for projects | Resource Manager

scenario: Which Google Cloud AI assistant helps admins explore resources and troubleshoot from the console?

options.text: Gemini Code Assist in the IDE
options.note: Helps write code, not explore projects.

explanation: Gemini Cloud Assist helps admins explore resources and troubleshoot from the Google Cloud console, including querying Cloud Asset Inventory. Gemini in Gmail and Code Assist in the IDE serve other purposes.

scenario: Which IAM feature grants access only when conditions are met, such as until a certain date?
explanation: IAM Conditions grant access only when attributes are met, such as time (an expiry date) or resource name. Basic roles and service account keys have no conditional logic.

scenario: Which command creates a Compute Engine VM?
explanation: gcloud compute instances create creates a VM, with --zone, --machine-type and --image-family as needed. gcloud run deploy and clusters create are for Cloud Run and GKE.

refs.title: gcloud compute instances create | Google Cloud SDK

scenario: A batch job can be interrupted and restarted. Which VM option is cheapest?
explanation: Spot VMs are the cheapest option for interruptible batch jobs, at the cost that Compute Engine can preempt them at any time. Standard VMs and 3-year commitments cost more.

scenario: Which resource defines the machine type, image and settings for VMs in a managed instance group?

options.text: A health check and backend service

explanation: An instance template defines the machine type, image and settings for VMs in a managed instance group. Templates are immutable, so create a new one to change settings.

scenario: Which managed instance group feature recreates VMs that fail an application health check?
explanation: Autohealing recreates VMs that fail an application health check; set an initial delay so VMs can boot before checks count. Autoscaling changes group size and rolling updates change templates.

refs.title: Set up an application-based health check and autohealing | Compute Engine

scenario: Which GKE mode manages nodes for you and bills per pod resource requests?
explanation: GKE Autopilot manages nodes for you and bills per pod resource requests, applying Google's best-practice configuration. Standard mode leaves node management to you.

scenario: Which command configures kubectl to access a GKE cluster?
explanation: gcloud container clusters get-credentials CLUSTER writes cluster credentials to your kubeconfig so kubectl can reach it. kubectl has no set-cluster --gke option.

refs.title: Install kubectl and configure cluster access | GKE

scenario: Which command deploys a container image to Cloud Run?
explanation: gcloud run deploy SERVICE --image IMAGE deploys a container to Cloud Run; --source builds from source. It is not an App Engine or functions command.

refs.title: Deploy container images to Cloud Run services

scenario: Which Cloud Storage class fits backups accessed about once a quarter?
explanation: Coldline fits data accessed about once a quarter (90-day minimum storage duration). Nearline is monthly with a 30-day minimum, Archive is yearly with 365 days, and Standard is for frequent access.

scenario: Which command copies a local file to a Cloud Storage bucket?
explanation: gcloud storage cp file.txt gs://BUCKET/ copies a local file into a bucket; gsutil cp also works but gcloud storage is recommended. mb makes buckets, and bq load targets BigQuery.

refs.title: Quickstart: Discover object storage with the Google Cloud CLI

scenario: Which database fits a lift-and-shift of a MySQL app needing a managed regional database?
explanation: Cloud SQL for MySQL is the managed, regional relational database suited to lifting and shifting a MySQL app (it also supports PostgreSQL and SQL Server). Spanner, Bigtable and Firestore have different data models.

refs.title: Cloud SQL overview | Cloud SQL for MySQL

scenario: Which storage option gives a VM a high-performance block disk that can be resized and snapshotted?

options.text: Local SSD attached to the VM

explanation: Persistent Disk or Hyperdisk provides block storage for VMs that can be resized and snapshotted; Hyperdisk lets you tune IOPS and throughput separately. Cloud Storage is object storage and Local SSD is ephemeral.

refs.title: Choose a disk type | Compute Engine

scenario: Which VPC mode lets you choose your own subnet ranges in each region?

options.note: Creates one subnet per region automatically.

explanation: A custom mode VPC lets you create your own subnets and ranges in each region. Subnets are regional while the VPC network itself is global; auto mode creates predefined subnets.

scenario: VMs without external IPs must reach the internet for updates. What should be configured?

options.text: Cloud NAT on a Cloud Router
An ingress firewall rule allowing all

explanation: Cloud NAT on a Cloud Router gives VMs without external IPs outbound-only internet access for updates. Peering and ingress firewall rules don't provide NAT.

scenario: VMs with only internal IPs need to reach Cloud Storage APIs. Which setting helps?

options.text: Private Google Access on the subnet
A public IP on each VM

explanation: Private Google Access, enabled per subnet, lets VMs with only internal IPs reach Google APIs and services such as Cloud Storage. Adding public IPs would work but defeats the intent.

refs.title: Private Google Access | Virtual Private Cloud

scenario: Which load balancer distributes HTTPS traffic globally to backends in multiple regions?

options.text: Regional internal passthrough Network Load Balancer

explanation: The global external Application Load Balancer distributes HTTPS traffic to backends in multiple regions through a single anycast IP address. Internal and regional passthrough balancers are regional.

scenario: Which load balancer handles internal TCP traffic between tiers in one region without proxying?

options.text: Regional internal proxy Network Load Balancer
options.note: Proxies connections instead of passing them through.

explanation: The internal passthrough Network Load Balancer handles internal TCP/UDP traffic in a region without proxying and preserves client IP addresses. Application and proxy balancers terminate connections.

scenario: Several projects must use subnets from one central network managed by a network team. What should be used?
explanation: Shared VPC lets a host project share subnets of one central network with service projects, managed by a network team. Peering every project or separate auto mode VPCs doesn't centralize control.

scenario: Which tool does Google recommend for infrastructure as code, now that Deployment Manager is retired?
explanation: Deployment Manager is retired; Google recommends Terraform, and Infrastructure Manager runs Terraform as a managed service. Cloud Scheduler and Build triggers aren't IaC tools.

scenario: Which BigQuery command loads a CSV file from Cloud Storage into a table?
explanation: bq load --source_format=CSV dataset.table gs://bucket/file.csv loads a CSV from Cloud Storage into a table; add --autodetect to infer the schema. bq query runs SQL instead.

scenario: Which messaging service decouples a web app from background workers?
explanation: Pub/Sub decouples a web app from background workers by passing messages through topics and subscriptions (push or pull). DNS, Cloud Armor and Persistent Disk aren't messaging services.

scenario: Which option deploys event-driven code that runs when a file lands in a bucket?

options.text: Cloud Run functions with a Cloud Storage trigger
A GKE DaemonSet that polls the bucket
A Cloud SQL trigger on an upload table

explanation: Cloud Run functions with a Cloud Storage trigger run code when an object lands in a bucket; Eventarc routes the events. Polling from GKE or a startup script is not event-driven.

scenario: Which Cloud SQL feature provides automatic failover to another zone?
explanation: Cloud SQL high availability uses a standby instance in a second zone for automatic failover. Read replicas scale reads and PITR restores data; neither fails over automatically as HA does.

refs.title: About high availability | Cloud SQL for MySQL

scenario: Which connectivity option links on-premises networks to a VPC over the internet with encryption?
explanation: Cloud VPN (HA VPN) links on-premises networks to a VPC over the internet with IPsec encryption, offering a 99.99% SLA with two tunnels. Dedicated Interconnect is a private physical link.

scenario: Which GKE object exposes a set of pods at a stable internal IP address?
explanation: A Kubernetes Service gives a set of pods a stable internal IP address (ClusterIP, with NodePort and LoadBalancer types). ConfigMap, Secret and PersistentVolumeClaim serve other purposes.

scenario: A data team needs managed Apache Airflow to schedule pipelines. Which service fits?

options.text: Managed Service for Apache Airflow (formerly Cloud Composer)

explanation: Managed Service for Apache Airflow (formerly Cloud Composer) runs managed Airflow to schedule pipelines. Cloud Scheduler and Cloud Tasks aren't workflow DAG orchestrators.

refs.title: Managed Airflow overview | Managed Service for Apache Airflow

scenario: Which storage service provides managed NFS file shares for VMs and GKE?
explanation: Filestore provides managed NFS file shares for VMs and GKE. Cloud Storage is object storage and Bigtable is a NoSQL database.

scenario: Which command creates a GKE Autopilot cluster?

options.text: gcloud container clusters create-auto NAME --region REGION

explanation: gcloud container clusters create-auto NAME --region REGION creates an Autopilot cluster, which is regional. The standard create command makes a Standard cluster.

scenario: Which agent should be installed on Compute Engine VMs to collect memory metrics and application logs?
explanation: The Ops Agent collects memory metrics and application logs from Compute Engine VMs, combining logging and monitoring collection. SSM Agent is AWS.

scenario: Which feature alerts when a public website stops responding?

options.text: Uptime check with an alerting policy

explanation: An uptime check with an alerting policy tests a public site from global locations and notifies you when it stops responding. Budgets and log sinks don't probe availability.

refs.title: Create public uptime checks | Cloud Monitoring

scenario: Which Cloud Logging feature routes logs to BigQuery for long-term analysis?
explanation: A log sink routes log entries to destinations such as BigQuery, Cloud Storage or Pub/Sub for long-term analysis. Log-based metrics count entries rather than exporting them.

scenario: Which audit log type is always on and records administrative changes like creating a VM?

options.note: Off by default for most services.

options.text: Firewall Rules Logging on all rules

explanation: Admin Activity audit logs are always on, free and can't be disabled; they record administrative changes such as creating a VM. Data Access logs record reads and are off by default for most services.

refs.title: Cloud Audit Logs overview | Cloud Logging

scenario: Which audit log type must usually be enabled to see who read objects in Cloud Storage?
explanation: Data Access audit logs record reads and must usually be enabled to see who read Cloud Storage objects (BigQuery Data Access logs are on by default). Admin Activity logs cover configuration changes only.

refs.title: Cloud Audit Logs overview | Cloud Logging

scenario: A VM needs a backup every night with 14 days of retention. What should be configured?

options.text: A snapshot schedule attached to the disk
A machine image created by hand weekly
An instance template with a disk image

explanation: A snapshot schedule attached to the disk takes automatic nightly snapshots with a retention period such as 14 days. Machine images made by hand or instance templates aren't scheduled backups.

refs.title: Create schedules for disk snapshots | Compute Engine

scenario: How can a managed instance group roll out a new instance template with no downtime?

options.text: Start a rolling update with maxUnavailable set to 0
Delete the group and recreate it
Stop all VMs first, then change the template
Change the zone of the group

explanation: A rolling update with maxUnavailable set to 0 replaces VMs gradually without reducing capacity, so there's no downtime; canary updates test a template on a subset. Recreating the group causes an outage.

refs.title: Automatically apply VM configuration updates in a MIG

scenario: Which command scales a GKE deployment to 5 replicas?
explanation: kubectl scale deployment web --replicas=5 sets the deployment to five replicas; a HorizontalPodAutoscaler adjusts replicas automatically. Resizing the cluster changes nodes, not replicas.

scenario: A Cloud Run service must handle traffic spikes but cap costs. Which setting helps?

options.text: Set a maximum number of instances
Increase the request timeout to 60 minutes

explanation: Setting a maximum number of instances caps Cloud Run scaling and therefore cost during traffic spikes. Minimum instances reduce cold starts but cost more.

refs.title: Set maximum instances for services | Cloud Run

scenario: How can traffic be split between two Cloud Run revisions to test a new version?

options.text: Create a second project for the new version
Change the container port on the new revision

explanation: Cloud Run splits traffic by assigning percentages to revisions, and tags give each revision a test URL. You don't need a second project or to delete the old revision.

refs.title: Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration | Cloud Run

scenario: Which tool searches and filters log entries in the console?
explanation: Logs Explorer is the console tool for searching and filtering log entries with the Logging query language. Metrics Explorer charts metrics, not log entries.

scenario: Which feature creates a metric from the count of matching log entries, like 'error' messages?
explanation: Log-based metrics create counters or distributions from matching log entries (for example 'error' messages), and alerting policies can use them. Sinks export logs instead.

scenario: How long does Cloud Logging keep logs in the _Default bucket by default?
explanation: The _Default log bucket keeps logs for 30 days by default; retention is configurable on custom buckets. It is not 7 days or forever.

scenario: A Cloud SQL instance needs to recover data to 10 minutes before an accidental delete. What should be used?
explanation: Point-in-time recovery restores a Cloud SQL instance to a chosen moment, such as 10 minutes before a delete. It needs automated backups plus binary logging (MySQL) or WAL archiving (PostgreSQL); read replicas don't undo deletes.

refs.title: Perform point-in-time recovery (PITR) | Cloud SQL for MySQL

scenario: Which GKE feature upgrades nodes automatically with minimal disruption?

options.text: Recreating the cluster for each version

explanation: Node auto-upgrade with maintenance windows keeps GKE nodes current with minimal disruption, and release channels control how quickly new versions arrive. Manual SSH or recreating clusters is unnecessary.

scenario: Which command lists running VMs in the current project?
explanation: gcloud compute instances list shows VMs in the current project; add --filter to narrow, such as status=RUNNING. gcloud projects list lists projects, not VMs.

scenario: Which tool shows a historical inventory of all resources and IAM policies across projects?
explanation: Cloud Asset Inventory keeps a historical inventory of resources and IAM policies across projects, with export to BigQuery. Monitoring dashboards and billing reports don't inventory resources.

scenario: Which service helps find latency bottlenecks across distributed requests?
explanation: Cloud Trace shows latency across distributed requests so you can find bottlenecks. Logging alone doesn't show request spans, and billing and asset tools aren't for latency.

scenario: A disk is running out of space on a VM. What's the least disruptive fix?

options.text: Resize the persistent disk, then grow the file system
Move the VM to a new region

explanation: Persistent disks can be resized while attached, so resize the disk and then grow the file system. This is far less disruptive than recreating the VM or changing machine type.

refs.title: Choose a disk type | Compute Engine

scenario: Which feature in Cloud Monitoring groups alerts so the right team gets notified?
explanation: Notification channels on alerting policies route alerts to the right people (email, SMS, Slack, PagerDuty, Pub/Sub). Log sinks and budgets aren't alert routing.

scenario: Which GKE feature adds nodes when pods can't be scheduled due to lack of resources?
explanation: The GKE cluster autoscaler adds nodes when pods can't be scheduled for lack of resources. The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler changes replica counts; Autopilot handles node scaling for you.

scenario: Which Cloud Storage feature deletes objects older than 365 days automatically?

options.note: Retain deleted objects; do not delete old ones.

explanation: Object Lifecycle Management rules delete or change the storage class of objects based on age, such as deleting after 365 days. Bucket Lock prevents deletion instead.

scenario: A Cloud Run service returns errors after a new deployment. What's the fastest way to restore service?

options.text: Route 100% of traffic back to the previous revision
Delete the service and redeploy from scratch
Increase the memory of the new revision
Disable logging on the new revision

explanation: Revisions are immutable, so routing 100% of traffic back to the previous Cloud Run revision restores service immediately. Redeploying from scratch is slower.

refs.title: Rollbacks, gradual rollouts, and traffic migration | Cloud Run

scenario: Which service manages database fleets and recommendations across Cloud SQL, AlloyDB and Spanner?
explanation: Database Center gives a fleet-wide view of Cloud SQL, AlloyDB and Spanner with health, security and performance recommendations. Query Insights covers a single instance's queries.

scenario: Which dashboard shows Google Cloud incidents that affect your specific projects?
explanation: Personalized Service Health shows incidents that affect your specific projects, and can alert you. The public status dashboard shows general Google Cloud status.

scenario: How can an admin SSH into a Linux VM using their IAM identity rather than managing SSH keys?

options.text: Copy keys into metadata for each user manually

explanation: OS Login ties Linux SSH access to IAM roles (with optional 2FA), so you don't manage SSH keys in metadata. Shared passwords and port 3389 (RDP) are the wrong approach.

scenario: A VM needs to read from a Cloud Storage bucket. What's the recommended way to give it access?

options.text: Attach a service account with a storage role
Copy a user's password to the VM
Make the bucket public for the VM's IP range
Download a service account key to the VM

explanation: Attach a service account with an appropriate storage role to the VM; it receives short-lived credentials from the metadata server. Copying passwords or downloading keys creates leakable secrets.

refs.title: Attach service accounts to resources | IAM

scenario: Why should service account keys be avoided when possible?

options.text: They're long-lived credentials that can leak
They can't be used outside Google Cloud

explanation: Service account keys are long-lived credentials that can leak. Prefer attached service accounts, impersonation or Workload Identity Federation; keys don't expire hourly or get required everywhere.

refs.title: Best practices for managing service account keys

scenario: Workloads running on AWS need to call Google Cloud APIs without service account keys. What should be used?

options.text: A service account key stored in AWS Secrets Manager
Cloud NAT with a static IP

explanation: Workload Identity Federation lets AWS workloads exchange their identity tokens for short-lived Google credentials, with no service account keys to store. A key stored in AWS Secrets Manager is still a long-lived key.

scenario: Which role lets a user act as a service account (impersonate it)?

options.text: Service Account Token Creator or Service Account User

explanation: Service Account Token Creator or Service Account User allows a principal to impersonate or act as a service account, avoiding the distribution of keys.

scenario: How do GKE workloads best access Google Cloud APIs securely?

options.text: Node service account keys in each pod

explanation: Workload Identity Federation for GKE maps Kubernetes service accounts to IAM principals so pods call Google APIs without keys. Embedding keys or API keys in images is insecure.

refs.title: About Workload Identity Federation for GKE

scenario: Which firewall rule direction controls traffic entering VMs?
explanation: Ingress rules control traffic entering VMs. VPC networks have implied rules that deny all ingress and allow all egress.

scenario: How can firewall rules target only web server VMs?

options.text: Use network tags or service accounts as targets
Apply them to the whole organization only
Use billing labels on the VMs

explanation: Firewall rules can target VMs by network tags or service accounts, so you can scope a rule to web servers only. Secure tags with Cloud NGFW policies add IAM-controlled targeting.

refs.title: Firewall policies and rules | Cloud Next Generation Firewall

scenario: Which feature applies firewall rules across many projects from the organization level?
explanation: Hierarchical firewall policies apply rules across many projects from the organization or folder level, and are evaluated before VPC firewall rules. Per-project rules don't centralize control.

refs.title: Firewall policies and rules | Cloud Next Generation Firewall

scenario: Which service protects internal web apps by checking user identity before allowing access?
explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) checks user identity and context before allowing access to internal apps, and IAP TCP forwarding secures SSH and RDP without public IPs. Cloud Armor and CDN don't verify identity this way.

scenario: Which service stores API keys and passwords for apps with versioning and IAM control?
explanation: Secret Manager stores API keys and passwords with versioning and IAM control; grant secretAccessor only to the workloads that need each secret. Metadata and public buckets are not secure.

scenario: Which encryption option lets a company control its own keys for BigQuery and Cloud Storage?

options.text: Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS
Disabling encryption at rest for the dataset

explanation: Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS let a company control the keys protecting BigQuery and Cloud Storage data. CSEK is another option for some services.

scenario: Which approach temporarily grants elevated access that expires automatically?

options.text: IAM Conditions with an expiry, or Privileged Access Manager
Disabling audit logs during the change

explanation: IAM Conditions with an expiry, or Privileged Access Manager just-in-time grants, give temporary elevated access that ends automatically. Permanent Owner or shared keys do not expire.

scenario: Which service limits data exfiltration from BigQuery and Cloud Storage to unauthorized networks?
explanation: VPC Service Controls creates perimeters around Google-managed services such as BigQuery and Cloud Storage to reduce data exfiltration. Cloud Armor and firewall egress rules don't cover API access.

scenario: A contractor needs read-only access to one bucket for a week. What's the best approach?

options.text: Grant Storage Object Viewer on the bucket with an IAM condition
Give them a service account key that expires

explanation: Grant Storage Object Viewer on that bucket with an IAM condition that expires in a week. Organization-wide Viewer is far too broad, and a public bucket exposes the data to everyone.

scenario: Which command grants a role to a user on a project?

options.text: gcloud iam roles create ROLE --project PROJECT --member EMAIL

explanation: gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT --member=user:EMAIL --role=ROLE adds a role binding on the project. Prefer groups over individual users where possible.

refs.title: IAM roles and permissions index | IAM

scenario: Which tool recommends removing unused permissions from principals?
explanation: IAM Recommender's role recommendations suggest removing unused permissions based on 90 days of usage. Policy Troubleshooter explains access decisions rather than recommending changes.

refs.title: Overview of role recommendations | Policy Intelligence

scenario: Which Cloud NGFW feature can block traffic to known malicious IP addresses?

options.text: Threat intelligence in firewall policy rules
Static routes to a null next hop

explanation: Cloud NGFW firewall policy rules can use threat intelligence to block traffic to or from known malicious IP addresses; Cloud NGFW Enterprise adds intrusion prevention.

refs.title: Firewall policies and rules | Cloud Next Generation Firewall

scenario: Which principle should guide role assignments for service accounts?

options.text: Grant Editor to every service account
Share one service account across all apps
Create keys for every service account

explanation: Least privilege guides service account roles: use separate service accounts per workload with only the roles they need. Granting Editor everywhere, sharing one account or creating keys violates it.

refs.title: Attach service accounts to resources | IAM
